content: Engram/TRAP reactivation literature (Nature Communications 2022 brain-wide engram mapping paper and related DG/CA1 studies) reports cFos+/tdTomato+ overlap percentages that are context-dependent: same-context (A-to-A) re-exposure produces significantly higher DG granule-layer overlap than different-context (A-to-B) exposure; CA1 neurons show repeated cFos expression across sessions (more promiscuous reactivation) unlike DG. Statistical significance of reactivation vs. chance is assessed via a hypergeometric-distribution overlap test comparing observed overlap counts to the expected chance overlap given population sizes. Exact percentage values for DG/CA1 same-context reactivation were not retrievable verbatim from search snippets in this session; classic Tonegawa-lab engram papers (Liu et al. 2012 Nature; Ramirez et al. 2013 Science; Tanaka et al. 2014 Science) are commonly cited in this literature as reporting matched-context reactivation fractions roughly in the 15-40% range with chance/different-context overlap around 5-15%, but this specific range is from training-data recall, not a directly quoted source this session -- flagged ASSUMED.
